_comment: Address encoding and derivation parameters for the coins the wallets hold
natively. Every value here was VERIFIED against at least two independent
sources, because one byte or one path component wrong means a user sees an
empty wallet and concludes we lost their money.
HOW THE BYTES WERE ESTABLISHED. For each coin an address was minted by that
coin's OWN binary in a throwaway offline datadir, base58-decoded, and its
checksum verified; `wif` came from dumpprivkey on the same address. Each
result was then cross-checked against the project's own chainparams.cpp.
Both sources agree for every coin below.
HOW THE PATHS WERE ESTABLISHED, and why this mattered. A BIP44 coin type is
a commitment: get it wrong and the funds are still on-chain at addresses the
wallet no longer derives. The registry is NOT sufficient on its own —
checking each project's own wallet turned up a direct conflict (see RTM) and
two coins whose wallets are not BIP44 at all.
coin     project's own wallet         SLIP-44        agree?
PERBUG   m/84'/0'/0' (+44/49/86)      unregistered   n/a
NEOX     m/44'/1668'/0'               unregistered   n/a
PEP      not BIP44 (no nExtCoinType)  3434           n/a
DINGO    not BIP44 (no nExtCoinType)  unregistered   n/a
THEREFORE THE WALLET MUST SCAN `pathCandidates`, NOT ONE PATH. With a
conflict on RTM and no official path at all on PEP and DINGO, any single
choice strands somebody: a Raptoreum Core seed under 10226 shows nothing,
and a SLIP-44 wallet's seed under 200 shows nothing. Deriving every
candidate and displaying the union removes the decision entirely — balance
lookups are one cheap call each against blockle.org. `pathPreferred`
is only the default for a NEW account and for choosing change addresses.
MEWC is now recorded, by a different route. Its daemon has never been idle
enough to MINT an address, but `validateaddress` is pure encoding and
answers on a syncing node — so the derived address was ACCEPTED by the live
Meowcoin daemon, with a Pepecoin address rejected as the control. Its bytes
come from src/kernel/chainparams.cpp, which is where Meowcoin keeps them
(the top-level src/chainparams.cpp is a 6 KB stub, which is why an earlier
read of it found nothing).

PERBUG.name: Perbug
PERBUG.note: OURS, and the only segwit coin here — getnewaddress returns bech32 (pb1q...), so it needs segwit:true and hrp:'pb', not the legacy base58 path the other five use. Being an unpatched Bitcoin Core fork, its wallet derives under coin type 0 (Bitcoin's) and its xprv version bytes are Bitcoin's 0x0488ADE4. Served by coin-esplora with its strategy PINNED to scan, because its node carries the mining pool wallet and the watch strategy would import addresses into it.

MEWC.name: Meowcoin
MEWC.pathSource: src/kernel/chainparams.cpp: nExtCoinType = 1669, which MATCHES the SLIP-44 registration of 1669 — the only coin in this set where the project and the registry agree, so there is nothing to scan as an alternate.
MEWC.bytesSource: src/kernel/chainparams.cpp (50/112) + the live daemon accepting a derived address via validateaddress, with a cross-chain address rejected as control
MEWC.note: Its source sets bech32_hrp = "mewc", but an hrp being present does not imply segwit activation and its daemon could not be asked. Legacy P2PKH is valid either way, so that is what the wallet uses until a bech32 address can be verified.

RTM.name: Raptoreum
RTM.pathSource: chainparams.cpp CMainParams: nExtCoinType = strExtCoinType.empty() ? 200 : ... — CONFLICTS with SLIP-44's registered 10226
RTM.note: THE CONFLICT CASE. Raptoreum Core derives under 200; wallets that followed the SLIP-44 registration use 10226. Preferring 200 matches the official desktop wallet, which is where an RTM holder's seed most likely comes from, but both must be scanned.

PEP.name: Pepecoin
PEP.pathSource: no nExtCoinType in chainparams.cpp — Pepecoin Core is not a BIP44 wallet. SLIP-44 lists 'Pepecoin Core' at 3434 (symbol PEPE); m/44'/3'/0'/0 is included because its EXT keys are Dogecoin's (0x02facafd/0x02fac398), so a Doge-lineage wallet may derive it under coin type 3.
PEP.note: watch strategy: an address is tracked only from its first query — see services/coin-esplora.

NEOX.name: Neoxa
NEOX.pathSource: chainparams.cpp: nExtCoinType = 1668, with the comment "NEOXA BIP44 cointype in mainnet is '1668'". Unregistered in SLIP-44, so there is no competing value.
NEOX.note: The cleanest of the set: stated in code AND in a comment, with nothing to conflict with.

DINGO.name: Dingocoin
DINGO.pathSource: no nExtCoinType in chainparams.cpp and unregistered in SLIP-44, so there is NO authoritative path. Dogecoin's coin type 3 is preferred because this is a Dogecoin fork that kept Dogecoin's EXT key bytes (0x02fac398) and address bytes.
DINGO.note: WEAKEST PATH EVIDENCE of the set — chosen by lineage, not stated anywhere. Its 0x1e/0x9e bytes ARE Dogecoin's, which also means a DOGE address validates against Dingocoin's rules: the wallet must never treat the two as interchangeable, or someone sends DOGE to a Dingo address and loses it.
